summary: Walker County, Alabama fire tower listed on TopoQuest at 672 ft; no source found dates it or confirms it still stands.

evidence.supports: Eastern U.S. Lookouts has a page for a lookout named High Hill
High Hill Fire Tower is in Walker County, at 672 ft elevation (672 ft MSL)
evidence.quote: High Hill Fire Tower is a tower located in Walker County, AL at N33.611221° W87.271945° (WGS84/NAD83) and at an elevation of 672 ft MSL.

evidence.supports: TopoQuest still lists a tower at the point; the listing does not show whether the structure stands today
evidence.quote: High Hill Fire Tower is a tower located in Walker County, AL at N33.611221° W87.271945° (WGS84/NAD83) and at an elevation of 672 ft MSL.

evidence.supports: Statewide: the first lookouts were platforms in trees
evidence.quote: In the early 20th century, the first lookouts were platforms in trees.

evidence.supports: Statewide: the forest service then built wooden towers of creosote wood
evidence.quote: Soon after, the forest service began erecting wooden towers built of creosote wood.

evidence.supports: Statewide: many early wooden towers were replaced by steel towers during the New Deal
evidence.quote: As far as we know, none of these still stand today, as many were replaced by steel towers during the New Deal.

evidence.supports: Fewer than 75 of these historic structures still stand in Alabama
evidence.quote: Today, however, there are probably less than 75 of these historic structures still standing in Alabama.

evidence.supports: Many are very unsafe and illegal to climb
evidence.quote: Many are looking worse for the wear, are very unsafe, and are illegal to climb.

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: Only two pages name this lookout: the Eastern U.S. Lookouts page (name only, no county or agency) and TopoQuest, a map-feature database that gives a point, the county and an elevation of 672 ft MSL; it is not a status record. The record coordinates (33.61115, -87.27183) agree with TopoQuest's point to within about 0.0001 degree. The record's county is null; TopoQuest's Walker County placement could fill it, but county is not a facts key, so it is flagged here rather than proposed as a correction. Two searches found no build date, builder, agency, owner or current status. Whether the structure still stands is not verified. Treat the story as a location record.
